text.p: Subaru of America Inc, a unit of Fuji Heavy Industries Ltd, said Monday it plans to introduce a new generation sport-utility vehicle for the 1998 model year.
The vehicle is based on a car platform and will be classified by the Environmental Protection Agency as a passenger car, Subaru said. Sport utility vehicles are typically classified as trucks.

"This new vehicle is built from the ground up as a true hybrid," said George Muller, president and chief operating officer of Subaru. "It embodies our philosophy of delivering a 'best of both' concept."
Subaru made the announcement at the North American International Auto Show.
The vehicle's name will be announced in the spring. It will go on sale in the United States later this summer.

Dimensions and specifications were not yet available. However, Subaru said the vehicle will be equipped with a four-cylinder 2.5 liter engine, a choice of four-speed automatic or five-speed manual transmissions, standard full-time all-wheel drive, four-wheel independent suspension, and a choice of either an L or S model.
A five-passenger vehicle, it will have ground clearance equivalent to the Subaru Outback but with shorter departure and approach angles, giving it more off-road capability, the company said.
The vehicle will be built at Fuji Heavy Industries' Gunma plant in Japan.
